note: Recorded live Claude investigation. Replayed tool calls run against the current database; claims are re-verified on replay.

hypotheses_considered.why: It accounts for 0.7035 of the excess (Q2). Its refunds are spread across six SKUs, not only HDPH-200 (Q7), so this is a problem with the partner rather than the product mix.
hypotheses_considered.hypothesis: The fulfillment partner SwiftShip-EU is driving the refund spike

hypotheses_considered.why: It accounts for 0.6345 of the excess and had a baseline rate of 0 (Q3). It is elevated at three partners besides SwiftShip-EU, including BlueDart-Intl at 37.5% and NorthPost at 40% (Q8), so the problem does not depend on the partner.
hypotheses_considered.hypothesis: The SKU HDPH-200 is driving the spike on its own

hypotheses_considered.why: EU accounts for 0.7862 of the excess (Q4), but its captures (44) almost match SwiftShip-EU's (45). It is probably the same population. I had no budget left to cross-check.
hypotheses_considered.hypothesis: The EU region is a separate cause

hypotheses_considered.why: Electronics accounts for 0.6912 of the excess (Q6) and probably reflects HDPH-200. I did not cross-check this.
hypotheses_considered.hypothesis: The electronics category is a separate cause

hypotheses_considered.why: The excess is spread fairly evenly across web, mobile and marketplace (Q5). That pattern points to an upstream cause that affects every channel, not to one channel.

final.hypothesis: There appear to be two independent causes: a problem with the fulfillment partner SwiftShip-EU (the main cause), and a problem with the product HDPH-200 that shows up across partners.
final.observed_anomaly: The refund rate was 21.51% (20 refunds out of 93 captures), compared with a 3.43% baseline.
final.explanation: SwiftShip-EU has a refund rate of 31.11%, compared with its 4.55% baseline, and accounts for 70.35% of the excess refunds. Within SwiftShip-EU, refunds are spread across several SKUs (for example, MUG-CLASSIC, LAMP-LED and TEE-ORG), which points to the partner rather than one product. Separately, HDPH-200 went from a 0 baseline to 37.93%. It is also elevated at BlueDart-Intl and NorthPost, so the product has its own problem. The EU region and the electronics category likely reflect these two causes rather than adding new ones.
final.uncertainty: I had no budget left to fetch refund reason codes, so I can't tell whether the cause is shipping damage, product defects or something else. I also did not confirm that EU and SwiftShip-EU are the same population, or that electronics is really HDPH-200. The sample sizes are small, from 12 to 45 captures per slice. I did not inspect any individual transactions.
